newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says Merck settles environmental case.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says Merck settles environmental case.

text.p: Merck and Co Inc has agreed to pay more than $1.8 million in penalties to settle allegations that a kelp processing plant it formerly owned in San Diego violated air pollution limits for several years, two federal government agencies said Thursday.

The U.S. Justice Department and the Environmental Protection Agency said the facility's current owner, Monsanto Co, also has agreed to install pollution control equipment to sharply reduce smog-causing emissions.

The settlement was filed in federal court in San Diego, the two agencies said. It resolved allegations that Merck, which owned the plant until February 1995, made several modifications without obtaining the necessary permits and failed to install the best available emission controls.
